text:
A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet. Everything you send goes through it in scrambled form, so people on the same Wi-Fi, or your internet provider, can't read it.

The tunnel ends at a VPN company's computer, which then visits websites for you. Those sites see that computer's address instead of yours, so you look like you're somewhere else.

It's handy on public Wi-Fi or for keeping your browsing private from your provider. It doesn't make you anonymous, though, because the VPN company can still see where you go, so pick one you trust.
